source: Numerics/Sampling/MCMC/Base/MCMCSampler.cs (the delegate constructor) + Numerics/Sampling/MCMC/Gibbs.cs; Numerics/Sampling/Bootstrap/Bootstrap.cs (the four delegate properties) @ 2a0357a
reference: Numerics @ 2a0357a. Two cases, each nesting two sub-blocks shaped exactly like a "callback"-kind case's construct/assertions: an "mcmc" block (group "mcmc", method "sample") and a "bootstrap" block (group "bootstrap", method "run"). The nesting is the point. Every other callback fixture pins ACCURACY against the real C# library at that file's relative tolerance; this file's job is the CROSS-LANGUAGE guarantee on the CALLBACK path, so EVERY assertion below is spelled mode "abs" with tol 0, i.e. bit equality in all four runners, not a tolerance. It is the callback layer's counterpart to fixtures/toolbox/toolbox_cross_language.json and fixtures/estimation/fit_cross_language.json. WHAT THE PACKAGES PROMISE AND WHERE IT STOPS: on the registry path every operation happens inside the shared C++ core, so a seeded run is bit-identical between R and Python by construction. On the callback path the draws still come from the core generator, but the log-density (or the proposal, or the statistic) is arithmetic the HOST language evaluates, and R and Python do not guarantee identical rounding for the same formula. MCMC amplifies that without mercy: one flipped accept-or-reject changes every state after it, so chains diverge outright rather than drift. Both callbacks used here are therefore built from + - * / and comparisons alone, with every summation written as an explicit loop rather than any language's sum()/mean()/Average() (R accumulates those in extended precision where C++, Python and C# accumulate in double). Arithmetic-only callbacks are IEEE-deterministic, so they reproduce exactly; a callback that calls log() or exp() need not, and the two worked examples (site/examples/14-custom-posterior, 15-custom-bootstrap) say so in prose rather than leaving it implied. WHY THESE TWO CONSTRUCTS AND NOT WIDER ONES: the constructs were chosen by measurement, not by taste. R and Python agree bit for bit on EVERY callback case in this directory, including the DEMCz two-parameter regression posterior of fixtures/callback/mcmc.json. They agree with the real C# library only where the arithmetic that produces the number lives in the CALLBACK rather than in the compiled core, because clang and gcc contract `a*b + c` into a fused multiply-add by default and .NET does not: on the DEMCz case that gap is 1.5e-14 on the posterior mean and 7e-15 on a late chain state, well inside every other fixture's rel 1e-12 but not zero. The Gibbs case has no such gap. Its recorded states are exact full-conditional draws, `lo + u * (hi - lo)` evaluated in the host language off the core generator, and its posterior mean, median and MAP are a plain sum, an order statistic and a maximum over those states, none of which the core can fuse. So this file pins the quantities that are bit-identical in all four runners and says here, in the open, which ones are not: posterior_sd and ess accumulate `d*d` inside the core and reproduce C#-vs-package to 1.4e-16 and 4.6e-14 rather than exactly, so they are deliberately absent below rather than pinned at a loosened tolerance. THE MCMC BLOCK IS THE GIBBS SAMPLER on purpose: it is the one sampler neither package could reach before this phase, because Gibbs requires a proposal delegate and the packages had no way to pass one. THE SECOND CASE, linear_model_contractible_arithmetic_short_exact, EXISTS TO MAKE ONE COMPILER FLAG DEMONSTRABLE. core/CMakeLists.txt compiles the C++ catalog (core/tests/fixture_callback_catalog.cpp) with -ffp-contract=off, because clang and gcc otherwise fuse `a*b + c` into a single multiply-add and the C++ counterpart of a callback then computes a different function from the R, Python and C# ones. The first case cannot detect that: the callbacks it names are comparisons (Mcmc_UniformWidthKernel) and index draws (Resample_Iid), neither of which has a product to fuse, and removing the flag left the entire fixture tree green. This case names arithmetic the compiler does fuse and pins it at tol 0, so removing the flag fails here. Both of its blocks work on the same straight line through the same eight observations: the mcmc block samples y = a + b*t under Mcmc_LinearKernel, the bootstrap block resamples those y and fits them with Fit_LinearTrend. Two assertions carry the demonstration, both measured by building the catalog each way (Apple clang 21, arm64). statistic[0], the intercept of the ORIGINAL fit, moves by about 50 ulp (0.03571428571428292 written against 0.035714285714283256 fused), because `ybar - slope * tbar` subtracts two nearly equal quantities and so amplifies a last-bit difference in the slope; map_fitness moves by 1 ulp, which is the whole size of the effect on a single kernel evaluation. THE MCMC SEED IS A MEASURED CHOICE rather than a decoration: 72% of the kernel's values over this proposal box differ between the fused and unfused forms, but map_fitness is the maximum over one particular chain, and at seed 12345 -- the seed the first case uses -- the state that wins it falls in the other 28%. Seed 22 is the nearest one where it does not. Nothing else in the mcmc block can move: Gibbs accepts unconditionally and Prop_UniformBox ignores the state it is handed, so the chain is a sequence of independent draws and the log-density's only mark on the run is the fitness recorded beside each state. WHAT THIS CASE DOES NOT PROVE: on x86-64 no compiler may emit a fused multiply-add unless FMA is enabled (-mfma, or -march=x86-64-v3 and up), so on a default Linux or Windows x86-64 build the flag is inert and removing it changes nothing here. The demonstration is real on arm64 and on any x86-64 build with FMA turned on. AN HONEST ODDITY IN ITS BOOTSTRAP BLOCK: statistic[0] is 0.036 while the resampled interval for that same quantity runs from 2.86 to 15.23. That is correct rather than broken -- an iid resample destroys the order the trend lives in, so a replicate's slope is near zero and its intercept near the sample mean, 9.0. The block pins arithmetic; it is not estimating a trend. EVERY expected value is EMITTER-READ from the real Numerics classes driven by tools/oracle_emitter, never a value computed by this repo's own C++.

callbacks.Mcmc_UniformWidthKernel: f(mu) = 0 when every |x - mu| <= 1 over x = {4.9, 5.1, 5.0, 5.2, 4.8}, else -infinity  [the same catalog callback fixtures/callback/mcmc.json documents: the log-likelihood of x_i ~ Uniform(mu - 1, mu + 1) with the normalizing term dropped. Comparisons only, so it cannot round differently anywhere]
callbacks.Prop_UniformConditional: proposal(parameters, prng) = lo + prng.NextDouble() * (hi - lo), lo = max(x) - 1 = 4.2, hi = min(x) + 1 = 5.8  [the same catalog callback fixtures/callback/mcmc.json documents, upstream's Gibbs.Proposal(double[], Random) shape: the EXACT full conditional of Mcmc_UniformWidthKernel under a flat prior, so every recorded state is an independent Uniform(4.2, 5.8) draw. One NextDouble per call, off the generator the sampler hands in]
callbacks.Resample_Iid: resample(data, parameters, prng) -> n draws of data[prng.Next(0, n)], n = data.Length  [the same catalog callback fixtures/callback/bootstrap.json documents: the ordinary nonparametric resample, every index drawn off the generator the replicate hands in]
callbacks.Fit_Mean: fit(data) -> [sum(data) / data.Length], summed in an explicit loop  [the same catalog callback fixtures/callback/bootstrap.json documents]
callbacks.Stat_Identity: statistic(parameters) -> parameters  [the same catalog callback fixtures/callback/bootstrap.json documents: the statistic IS the fitted parameter, so the interval is an interval on the mean]
callbacks.Mcmc_LinearKernel: f(a, b) = -0.5 * sum((y_i - a - b*t_i)^2) over t = 1..8 and y = {2.1, 3.9, 6.2, 7.8, 10.1, 12.2, 13.8, 16.1}, accumulated in an explicit loop  [the same catalog callback fixtures/callback/mcmc.json documents. The second case's kernel, and the CONTRACTIBLE one: `y - a - b*t` and `acc + r*r` are both the shape a C++ compiler fuses into a multiply-add]
callbacks.Prop_UniformBox: proposal(parameters, prng) = [lo_j + prng.NextDouble() * (hi_j - lo_j)] for lo = (-1, 1.5), hi = (1, 2.5)  [the two-parameter member of the proposal catalog. An INDEPENDENCE proposal: it ignores the state it is handed, so with Gibbs accepting unconditionally the chain is a sequence of independent draws from that box. The box brackets the least-squares fit of Mcmc_LinearKernel's eight observations (intercept ~0.036, slope ~1.998) and sits strictly inside the priors]
callbacks.Fit_LinearTrend: fit(data) -> [ybar - slope * tbar, slope], slope = sum(dt*dy) / sum(dt*dt) over t = 1..n, in an explicit loop  [the contraction-bearing member of the bootstrap catalog: every accumulation is `acc + a*b` and the intercept then subtracts two nearly equal quantities, so the fused and unfused values differ well past the last bit. sum(dt*dt) depends only on n, so no resample can make the fit fail]
